title: A Broad Line-width, Compact, Millimeter-bright Molecular Emission Line Source near the Galactic Center
question: What is the compact, broad-linewidth (FWHM ~160 km/s), millimeter-bright source G0.02467-0.0727 (MUBLO) near the Galactic Center, and which physical scenarios could explain it?

data.arrays: 12m array for ACES and 2012 data; 7m array for 2017.1.01185.S; ACES also has 7m and total power (TP) data
data.angular_resolution: ACES continuum spw33+35 beam 1.538 x 1.306 arcsec (PA -59.907 deg); 2012 continuum 2.359 x 1.397 arcsec; 2017 7m Band 7 continuum 4.337 x 2.519 arcsec
data.sensitivity: continuum RMS 0.2 mJy/beam (ACES spw33+35); 0.4 mJy/beam (2012); 8.8 mJy/beam (2017 Band 7); per-spw line RMS 2.6-3.4 mJy/beam (channel width not stated)

what.value: Dust opacity for protostellar cores used for the mass estimate

evidence.quote: Adopting a standard dust opacity for protostellar cores (cite: Ossenkopf1994), assuming T=20 K and gas-to-dust mass ratio 100

what.value: Spitzer and Herschel surface brightnesses used as SED upper limits

evidence.quote: From the Spitzer (cite: Ramirez2008; Carey2009) and Herschel (cite: Traficante2011) data, we adopt the surface brightness at the position of the source as an upper limit

what.value: Enhanced H2 cosmic-ray ionization rates adopted in Meudon PDR models

evidence.quote: We adopt enhanced (compared to that in Galactic disk GMCs) H$_2$ cosmic-ray ionization rates (cite: Indriolo2015).

what.value: Protostar SED model grid used to test central-source properties

evidence.quote: Using the (cite: Richardson2024) update to the (cite: Robitaille2017) grid, we searched for models consistent with either of the two ALMA millimeter detections

what.value: Stellar proper motions near the source

evidence.quote: We also checked the surrounding sources from (cite: Shahzamanian2022) within $r<10\ensuremath{''}$

what.value: Continuous-shock chemical model grids for SO/SiO ratios

evidence.quote: (cite: DutkowskaVermarien2024) explored a wide range of continuous shock model parameters

what.value: Alternative dust opacities (supernova power law, VY CMa extrapolation, Draine 2006 range)

evidence.quote: (cite: Draine2006) gives a range of dust opacities from $0.0003<\kappa_\mathrm{102 GHz} < 0.03$ cm$^2$ g$^{-1}$

recipe.method: Re-ran CASA imaging with the ALMA pipeline parameters, fixing diverged cleans and imaging windows left un-imaged or at full spectral resolution; archival 2012 and 2017 data re-imaged with the ACES pipeline

recipe.goal: Fit line profiles at the peak position
recipe.method: Extract spectra at the peak emission position and fit Gaussian profiles, with foreground absorption components for CS 2-1 and SO 2(3)-1(2)
2D Gaussian fits to continuum and integrated-intensity images in all three data sets; beam-deconvolved sizes reported
Collapse the red and blue sides of the SO 2(3)-1(2) cube into moment-0 images, excluding the extended cloud near 45 km/s, and fit their positions
key_parameters: Red 64 to 152 km/s, blue -68 to 34 km/s

recipe.goal: Continuum spectral index and dust mass
recipe.method: Assume a single point source, derive spectral index between Band 3 and Band 7, and estimate mass from both frequencies with an optically thin dust formula
key_parameters: T = 20 K, kappa = 0.002 cm^2/g at 102 GHz and 0.018 cm^2/g at 350 GHz
assumptions: Ossenkopf (1994) dust opacity, T=20 K, gas-to-dust mass ratio 100, D = 8 kpc

recipe.goal: Constrain dust temperature from the SED
recipe.method: Use Spitzer and Herschel surface brightness as upper limits and overlay modified blackbodies with beta = 1.5
assumptions: Power-law opacity kappa proportional to nu^beta with beta = 1.5

recipe.goal: LTE rotational diagram of SO and column densities
recipe.method: Rotational diagram from two detected SO transitions and an upper limit on a third; model spectra overlaid with CS and SO2 columns scaled at the fitted temperature
assumptions: LTE, justified by the dust-derived density; same temperature for other molecules

recipe.method: Grid of RADEX one-zone models, using the SO 2(3)-1(2)/2(2)-1(1) ratio and a lower limit on the SO 2(3)-1(2) intensity from filling factor <= 1
assumptions: Dust-based H2 number density combined with the models to rule out low-density solutions

recipe.goal: Chemical modelling of SO/CS and SO/SiO ratios
recipe.method: Meudon PDR constant-density slabs for line and column density ratios; UCLCHEM time-dependent collapse models for SO/SiO
key_parameters: Meudon grid: n_H 2e5 and 2e7 cm^-3, G0 = 1e3, zeta_CR 2e-17 to 2e-14 s^-1, A_V,max 20/200/800
UCLCHEM grid: final n_H 1e5, 1e6, 1e7 cm^-3; T 15 and 50 K

recipe.goal: Compare dust SED with protostar model grid
recipe.method: Search the Robitaille/Richardson grid for models within 25% of the ALMA flux densities in 5000 au apertures and below the 24 and 70 micron upper limits

answer_key.quantity: Line FWHM and centroid velocity, CS 2-1
Line FWHM and centroid velocity, SO 2(2)-1(1)

evidence.quote: The separation is 2000$\pm200$ au assuming $d=8$ kpc over a 112 $\mathrm{km~s}^{-1}$ difference, resulting in a gradient of 11,000 $\mathrm{km~s}^{-1}$ pc$^{-1}$.
the spectral index is $\alpha=3.25\pm0.06$ (statistical) $\pm0.17$ (systematic, adopting 10% calibration uncertainty)
The column density, $N(H_2)\sim4\times10^{23}$ $\mathrm{cm}^{-2}$, corresponds to extinction $A_K\approx20$.
the energy in the gas is very large, $E_{kin} = 5\times10^{48}\mathrm{~erg}
the allowed range of dust temperatures is $15 \lesssim T \lesssim 50$ K

answer_key.quantity: LTE excitation temperature from SO lines

evidence.quote: The temperature from the SO 2(3)-1(2) to 2(2)-1(1) line ratio is $T=14.1\pm 1.4$ K

answer_key.uncertainty: systematic dominated by temperature, possibly more than an order of magnitude

answer_key.quantity: Column densities of CS, C34S, SO2, 34SO

evidence.quote: we obtain column densities N(CS)=$10^{15}$ $\mathrm{cm}^{-2}$, N(C$^{34}$S)=$1.2\times10^{14}$ $\mathrm{cm}^{-2}$, N(SO$_2$)=$2\times10^{16}$ $\mathrm{cm}^{-2}$, and N($^{34}$SO)=$5\times10^{14}$ $\mathrm{cm}^{-2}$

answer_key.quantity: Abundances relative to H2, SO and CS
Allowed N(SO) and T in LTE models given R32
Meudon PDR density and CRIR range matching SO/CS

answer_key.value: 10^4 < L < 10^4.7 Lsun and 3 < M_gas(<5000 au) < 28 Msun

evidence.quote: The 3$\sigma$ upper limit is $<2.8\times10^{-5}$ counts/s in the 3-8 keV band, equivalent to $S_{X}<7\times10^{-16}$ erg $\mathrm{s}^{-1}$$\mathrm{cm}^{-2}$ assuming a $\gamma=2$ power-law spectrum.

score_reason: Data come from the ALMA archive and the spectral and continuum measurements are given in tables with numeric values, but imaging parameters, fitting setup and several analysis choices are not stated and no code is released.
rediscovery_reason: Archival data, a short analysis recipe (Gaussian line fits, 2D Gaussian fits, spectral index, dust mass, LTE diagram) and numeric results in tables allow a check of the main measurements, though imaging details must be inferred.
